summary: Guidance on batching & route-weighting to prevent 429s from multi-call reranker workflow
description:
Issue summary: Customer Textlytics is seeing repeated 429s during peak traffic windows when their application issues a chain of small synchronous reranker calls per user query (avg 6 calls/query). They are on a Dedicated pool and report the Console shows available tenant burst credits, but the requests are throttled at the route level.

Impact: Intermittent user-facing errors; their search latency spikes and ~8% of queries return 429s during daily 09:00-11:00 UTC window. Business impact: search downtime for paying customers and degraded conversion for query sessions.

Environment: Dedicated pool backed by us-east cluster (gpu-p4d). Traffic pattern: short-lived connections, high concurrency from a serverless fleet that fans out rerank calls per web request.

Customer asks: 1) How to configure Redwood to reliably prioritize low-latency rerank calls vs background batch traffic? 2) Best-practice to reduce per-query 429s (batching, route-weight, concurrency limits)? 3) Any Console or API knob we should change on Dedicated to align observed quota with enforcement?

Expected behaviour: Route-level weights and tenant burst capacity should allow the low-latency reranker RPCs to proceed without sudden 429s when tenant-level credits are reported available.

Actual behaviour: Even with tenant credits available in the Console, individual route requests are being counted against a per-route concurrency/quota window causing 429s.

Attachments: request ids in logs, sample client call pattern, screenshots (uploaded to support ticket attachments).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Dedicated API key scoped to a single tenant and route for reranking (key used by serverless workers).
2) From 100 concurrent worker processes, issue user requests where each request makes 6 sequential reranker calls (small inputs).
3) Observe console showing tenant burst credits not fully depleted, but API returns 429s for a subset of calls.
4) Temporarily scale down background batch job to zero and re-run the traffic pattern to confirm the 429 drop rate.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial triage by Support—symptoms consistent with per-route concurrency/quota window exhaustion despite tenant-level credits.
Checked Console: tenant burst credit shows ~70-90 available during the window. No recent quota changes logged for this tenant.
Heap of short-lived connections from serverless fleet seems to create high instantaneous concurrency on the rerank route, which may be hitting route isolation limits.

Hypothesis: Per-route token bucket/refill window is configured shorter/smaller than tenant window; rapid multi-call fanout from each user query causes route window exhaustion and 429s even when tenant credit remains.
comments: Support (Mar 10) - Ayesha Kaur: Thanks for the reproduction steps and logs. We'll validate route vs tenant accounting and check that the Dedicated pool's route weighting is configured to favor your rerank route. Please provide a sample of the client-side call pattern (timestamps and counts per second).

Customer (Mar 10) - Textlytics (Emma Li): Uploaded a 30s capture of production traffic and the sample SDK trace. The pattern shows bursts of 600 calls/sec across 100 workers, where each user query fans out to 6 rerank calls in immediate succession.

SRE (Mar 11) - Marcus Nguyen: Confirmed route isolation rules applied on the pool. Observed short-window exhaustion for the 'rerank-v1' route (config: concurrency_window=10s, per-route-burst=80). Tenant-level burst is larger (per-tenant-burst=1000) but not applied when per-route window is exhausted. Recommend either batching client calls or adjusting route weights.

Eng (Mar 11) - Liam O'Connor: Proposed action: 1) Temporary mitigation: increase per-route-burst to 400 and widen concurrency_window to 30s for rerank-v1 on Textlytics' dedicated pool (requires controlled rollout). 2) Long-term: recommend client-side batching / multiplexing so a single request contains multiple items to rerank, reducing per-query RPC count. Shared RFC/guide link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SUPPORT/pages/4356

Support (Mar 12) - Ayesha Kaur: Shared a config snippet and step-by-step guide for Textlytics to test the per-route-burst change in staging before applying to prod. Asked customer to confirm whether changing client batching is feasible on their roadmap.
resolution: Workaround provided: suggested temporary per-route config increase (per-route-burst -> 400, concurrency_window -> 30s) for rerank-v1 on their Dedicated pool and guidance on client batching to reduce RPC fanout. Next steps: schedule a controlled config rollout in a maintenance window, and customer to evaluate batching implementation. Case remains open until config change validated in prod.
